The inane idea that "America" has ever been about freedom is one of the biggest cultic, true-believing articles of supremacist pseudo-faith there ever was. Right up there with believing that churches and religion have something to do with God.

A state is a monopoly on legitimized violence.

A government is the institution a state uses to control a population by means of violence and threat of violence, aka "penalty" and "punishment".

If you're serious about freedom, the first thing we need to do is eliminate the state and the government and abandon the idea of "rule of law" and the very idea of "governing" itself, because there can be no such thing as either except by legitimizing violence in order to force people to do what they might not want to do.

These things are no longer debatable -- not intelligently, at least.

There is NO evidence whatsoever -- AND NEVER HAS BEEN -- that states and governments are necessary, let alone that "chaos will ensue" without them. NONE.

There are OODLES of evidence that the most horrific, destructive, and deadly chaos ever loosed on Earth would never have happened except that states through their governments created and inflicted it.

The fact is: 98% of human suffering on Earth has been the doing of parasite classes that use states and their governments to subjugate the vast majority of people while, at the same time, those very law-slaves swear to fucking God that states and governments (and parasite classes, for that matter) are there to "protect" them from chaos. That belief is itself evidence of deep, generalized, socialized, and normalized psychosis.

On the other hand, the evidence that we do not need states and governments (and parasite classes, for that matter) is overwhelming. Since we emerged, 95% (and that's conservative) of homo sapiens have lived completely free of state-as-violence-monopolies control.

Think about it yourself. How many hours a week do you spend complying with laws and law enforcers, behaving as they demand when you'd do (or refrain from doing) just the opposite if they didn't demand it? How much do they change what you do from what you actually want to do? If there were no states, governments, laws, and parasite classes, would you become a less good, more evil person?

And remember: your impulse to say that the world would be a much more violent, far less safe place without states and governments and laws and parasite classes is BASELESS. Believing that, if everyone could just do as they pleased, other people would suddenly become less good and more evil is BASELESS. YOU have no evidence to support those beliefs. None. Zero. Zilch. Nada.

Those beliefs have no more basis or support than Russell's teapot.

What's more, they're evidence of YOUR own "moral" supremacism -- which is, in fact, immoral.

1. I'd disagree, not that humans **would be good** (as if the only factors involved are circumstantial/environmental), but that **humans are good, naturally, inherently, by the archetypal design of our psychology** and that it takes a shitload of influence/abuse/manipulation/gaslighting/existential threat to get us to diverge from that design.

2a - 2c: I really don't see a material difference between those 3. Clarify if you would. As it stands, I disagree with the assumption evident in the wording that humans have not, over and over since the Big Change (whatever it was) , **already** proven incontestably that they have the ability to do what you're asking about because they've already, actually done just that. Most people have the opposite impression because they're woefully ignorant of the many, many places and times where different groups did just that, to the tune of many hundreds of millions of people involved over thousands of years. Look up "Zomia" for a start. You're asking a question that's already been roundly answered. The question also denies/is oblivious to the fact that pre-Big Change, humans were universally almost completely violence-free. So, why is it a question to you at all?

Bottom line, you're working on the basis of assumptions and myths that are gradually being controverted, and the shift in archaeological and anthropological evidence creating the shift has been uncovered now for at least the last 50 years. Just gotta upgrade your knowledge corpus, man.

I don't "think" this actual, present world is merely capable of correcting the shit that so many take as normal and necessary and inevitable, I have no doubt that it's inevitable.

Instead, though, of challenging me to offer info that challenges/contradicts the myths you've been treating as foregone conclusions, I'm going to encourage you to do some digging and thinking, because you're asking me questions that amount to "Is it possible to find water to drink?" while you're standing next to an ancient freshwater lake. The question really isn't whether it's possible. It's why, when the evidence is all around you -- just not included in your indoctrination -- are you asking these questions?

comment.body:
// Bottom line: humans behave differently under different conditions. Violence results under certain conditions (external and internal) and not others. Yes, it is human nature to become violent under those conditions. But what about the hugely more plentiful conditions under which human nature is cooperative, mutually supportive, loving, and constructive? 

...This suggests that historical humans experienced 10× more violence per capita than prehistoric humans.... Here are the conditions that changed, and ALL of them are human-caused—so, they can be human-corrected... //

So would you agree with these statements?

1. If conditions were good (plentiful resources, etc), humans would be good (loving, kind, non-violent, etc).
2a. Humanity as a whole has the demonstrated ability to correct these human-caused problems.
2b. Humanity as a whole has the innate ability to eventually correct these human-caused problems.
2c. Humanity as a whole has the ability to learn and eventually correct these human-caused problems.

If not, how would you state your position or understanding of human nature / what humans are capable of?

And my next question would be, do you really think this world -- this actual world full of humans that currently exists -- is capable of that? Do you think individuals or small communities are capable of it, and under what conditions (what does it take for the individual or a group of people to succeed at being "good, loving, non-violent humans")?

comment.body:
//I didn't assume that's what you meant, and I wasn't accusing you of SAYING it so much as asking IF you were IMPLYING it.//

Cool, gotcha. As a standing note, in discussions like this I **do not imply**. Nothing to read between the lines. I do my best to say exactly what I mean and stand behind it exactly as I said it. If you find something vague or equivocal, my bad -- just ask me and I'll make it explicit and clear. A lot of people in the past have taken convos in some really bizarre directions because they just can't accept that I intended and meant something I didn't actually say. That's been happening less and less though. Grateful for that.

//
Meanwhile... look at your narrative. When you deny that we can each believe whatever we want, using the REASON that it's not possible or allowed, BECAUSE we are constrained by reality... and then you say to deny reality is to be psychotic (to break from reality)... What else are you saying by that?
//

I think that's a misread. Which statement(s) exactly are you referring to?

I took pains to make a sharp distinction between the questions of whether we're "allowed" to believe what we want and whether we are going to allow people to believe what they want. Did you get that part? 

It's not me that says a break from reality constitutes psychosis, it's the psychologists. 

Like I already said, I don't do insinuation, implied "what else I'm saying". Plus, you're the one who suspects "what else" -- so please reveal your suspicion. "What else" do you suspect I might have meant. Just sitting here, I don't have a clue.

Ah! Hadn't quite gotten there. No, I'm not saying "if we disagree then one of us is psychotic?" That would be pretty stupid, wouldn't it? I won't deny that I can sometimes be stupid, even extremely stupid -- just not that kind of stupid.

It will help from now on if you'd quote verbatim the phrase, sentence, or passage you're referring to when objecting or asking questions. It will spare crosstalk resulting from me guessing wrong what you have in mind.

I take it you're referring to the following?

//
So, no, you don't have the freedom to believe what you want unconstrained by reality, because breaking from reality constitutes psychosis. You and I reside in the same universe, so that's our common ground. It isn't subject to what we want to believe, and it doesn't change simply because we want to believe X, Y, or Z about it. Strictly speaking, you even have the freedom to be psychotic. But why would you want to? In other words, neither of us has the freedom to escape from the real situation we find ourselves in: residing in the same shared universe. That's why we call breaking from it "psychosis".
//

I'm not sure how you got "if we disagree then one of us is psychotic" from that, though. It will take a little work to read that and understand it, but it says nothing of the sort, nor does it imply or insinuate it. But maybe I need to hear from you how you're reading it. It's not uncommon for me to miss a possible interpretation that I didn't intend.

The point of that paragraph and the point of bringing the topic up at all is that, "... he's given us the freedom to say that. Given you the freedom to believe what you want, and me the freedom to believe what I want." is disembodied. It's a belief that exists in a conceptual vacuum, ignoring fundamental aspects of real life in the real world that would be its context, i.e., that would embody it. All I'm doing is shining some light on the context.

Remember Ra's al Ghul: “Mind your surroundings!”  😁

“Kangaroo court” doesn't even come close to this one. 

This is turning out to be par for the course and, as despicable as it might be, in the long run, these excesses of legal abuse need to be demonstrated on the record so that no question remains about their Insidious nature.

At the end of the day, this is all going to add up to a damning, incontestable condemnation -- not only of our current systems, but of the rationales and paradigmatic assumptions and principles by which they were designed and established. It will be not only a wholesale rejection and discarding of the systems and their designs themselves, but of the blatantly anti-human and anti-life intentions and motivations and purposes that we’ll certainly see inevitably led to the shitshow we’re witnessing now.

comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
Loved this right up to the close. Excellent piece.

Yes, there will be a final revolution, a decisive unmasking. Definitely. Absolutely. This current fiasco of straight-up madness isn't going to last forever. We’re watching it crumble now.

The cynical nihilism that was possible in the past reached its expiration date with postmodernism. What we’ve had since then has been the final scramble of the Wizards who, far more psychotic and evil than in Oz, still hide behind curtains manipulating spectacular lies. A pathetic and despicable bunch of Wile E. Coyotes, suspended, legs spinning before the inevitable plunge to the canyon floor. Headless chickens feverishly eeking out those last few bits of scratch.

I’m not even slightly kidding.

Boomers and Gen X will yield—by defeat or by death—to Millennials, but especially to Gen Z and Gen Alpha. 

Millennials began the transition. Nothing their elders and ancestors taught them made any fucking sense, and they started recognizing it. 

Gen Z has no doubt about it. 

Gen Alpha is aptly named, because they’re the first who will begin figuring out the alternatives to the fucking massive fiasco that these last 5,000 - 15,000 years have been, having rejected its very foundations: so-called “civilization”.

Just you watch.
